content.one_sentence_role: Turns pointwise equality on a seminorm sphere into a compactly supported Lipschitz perturbation.
content.natural_language_statement:
Fix $n\geq1$, and let $p$ be a continuous real seminorm on $\mathbb R^n$ whose closed unit ball $K=\{x:p(x)\leq1\}$ is compact. Let $F,G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^N$ be globally Lipschitz and satisfy $F(x)=G(x)$ whenever $p(x)=1$. For a fixed increasing selection $s=\{s_1<\cdots<s_n\}$ of output coordinates, put $\pi_s(y)=(y_{s_1},\ldots,y_{s_n})$ and $M_s(f)=\det(\pi_s\circ Df)$. Then
$$\int_KM_s(F)(x)\,dx=\int_KM_s(G)(x)\,dx.$$
content.assumptions:
There are constants $C_F,C_G\geq0$ for which
$$\|F(x)-F(y)\|_\infty\leq C_F\|x-y\|_\infty,\qquad
\|G(x)-G(y)\|_\infty\leq C_G\|x-y\|_\infty\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb R^n).$$
The other hypotheses are continuity of $p$, compactness of $\{p\leq1\}$, and pointwise equality $F(x)=G(x)$ on $\{p=1\}$. No smoothness or strict convexity of that sphere, Sobolev trace hypothesis, or separate definiteness assumption on $p$ is added.
content.conclusion: The integrals of the same signed, increasingly ordered maximal minor agree on $K$. Each integral is finite by the Lipschitz derivative bound on the compact set.
content.proof_summary: Extend the boundary-zero difference by zero, prove its Lipschitz bound across the sphere, and apply the compact-perturbation identity to a patched map.

proof_steps.text:
Put $u=F-G$ and define $u_0(x)=u(x)$ on $K$, $u_0(x)=0$ outside. The map $u$ is $(C_F+C_G)$-Lipschitz and vanishes on $\{p=1\}$. If $x\in K$ and $y\notin K$, continuity of $p$ along the segment from $x$ to $y$ supplies $z=(1-t)x+ty$, with $0\leq t\leq1$, such that $p(z)=1$. For $p(x)=1$ take $z=x$. Since $\|x-z\|=t\|x-y\|$, the mixed-side estimate is
$$\|u_0(x)-u_0(y)\|=\|u(x)-u(z)\|\leq(C_F+C_G)\|x-z\|\leq(C_F+C_G)\|x-y\|.$$
The same-side cases follow from the bound for $u$ or from both values being zero; reversing $x,y$ handles the other mixed case. Thus $u_0$ is globally Lipschitz with this constant. Its topological support satisfies $\operatorname{supp}u_0:=\overline{\{x:u_0(x)\ne0\}}\subseteq K$, because $K$ is closed. It is therefore compact.

Let $H=G+u_0$. Then $H=F$ on $K$ and $H=G$ outside. Apply the Lipschitz compact-perturbation theorem with base $G$, perturbation $u_0$, and the fixed $s$. The hypotheses just verified give
$$\int_{\mathbb R^n}(M_s(H)-M_s(G))=0.$$
This difference is integrable: its restriction to the compact support is a difference of integrable Lipschitz minors, and it vanishes outside that support.

To compare derivatives, use local equality, rather than merely equality at one point. On the open set $\{p<1\}$, $H$ agrees locally with $F$, hence $DH=DF$. On the open complement of $K$, $H$ agrees locally with $G$, hence $DH=DG$. The excluded set is $\{p=1\}$. The seminorm gauge identity identifies it with the frontier of $\{p<1\}$; this set is convex and contains a neighborhood of $0$ by continuity and the positive radius. The convex-frontier Haar-measure theorem therefore gives $|\{p=1\}|=0$. These are the hypotheses used by the linked private sphere-null lemma.

The local identities from Step 3 give
$$M_s(H)-M_s(G)=M_s(F)-M_s(G)\quad\text{almost everywhere on }K,$$
and $M_s(H)-M_s(G)=0$ on $K^c$. The integrable difference from Step 2 can therefore be split as
$$\begin{aligned}
0&=\int_{\mathbb R^n}(M_s(H)-M_s(G))\\
 &=\int_K(M_s(H)-M_s(G))+\int_{K^c}(M_s(H)-M_s(G))\\
 &=\int_K(M_s(F)-M_s(G))+0\\
 &=\int_KM_s(F)-\int_KM_s(G).
\end{aligned}$$
The last line uses the integrability of each Lipschitz minor on compact $K$. This proves the claimed equality.

content.lean_realization_notes: The sphere has measure zero for a specific reason: it is the frontier of the open convex seminorm ball, which is a neighborhood of the origin. Compactness of a general set would not by itself imply that its boundary has measure zero.
